title: Maximin Robust Bayesian Experimental Design
claim: Nominal Bayesian design is overconfident and miscalibrated; lowering alpha in the robust objective restores calibration and shifts realized information gains.
layout: 4 plots: two stacked histograms left, two coverage curves right
description: A row of four grayscale plots. At left, two stacked histograms (Linear Regression on top, A/B Testing below) show frequency of realized information gain. Light-gray nominal bars sit to the right of darker robust bars, with the robust distribution shifted lower and narrower. A legend labels Nominal and Robust. At right, two calibration plots (Linear Regression and A/B Testing) show actual versus expected coverage. Five curves for alpha from 1.0 to 0.056 run from light to dark gray, with a dotted diagonal marking perfect calibration. In linear regression, the nominal curve falls far below the diagonal and the smallest-alpha curve nearly hugs it. In A/B testing, the curves fan out around the diagonal. The eye goes first to the histograms and the fanned curves.
caption: Comparison of nominal and robust formulations for linear regression and A/B testing. Left: histograms of realized information gains under nominal (α = 1.0) and robust (α = 0.056) assumptions. Right: expected vs. actual coverage for varying values of α. Nominal posteriors are clearly overconfident; calibration improves for values α < 1. Data obtained from 104 experiments.
abstract: We address the brittleness of Bayesian experimental design under model misspecification by formulating the problem as a max--min game between the experimenter and an adversarial nature subject to information-theoretic constraints. We demonstrate that this approach yields a robust objective governed by Sibson's $Î±$-mutual information~(MI), which identifies the $Î±$-tilted posterior as the robust belief update and establishes the RÃ©nyi divergence as the appropriate measure of conditional information gain. To mitigate the bias and variance of nested Monte Carlo estimators needed to estimate Sibson's $Î±$-MI, we adopt a PAC-Bayes framework to search over stochastic design policies, yielding rigorous high-probability lower bounds on the robust expected information gain that explicitly control finite-sample error.
